# Registry fix — report

Two changes, both in the working tree, nothing committed.

## 1. The generated file now defends itself

`libs/backend/task-specs/src/lib/registry-generator.service.ts` — `render()` now emits
four HTML-comment header lines instead of one, all static text (no wall-clock, so
determinism holds; the `Last content change` line is still `max(updated)` as before).

The added lines say, in the file itself:

- **DERIVED, NOT AUTHORITATIVE** — a snapshot, arbitrarily stale, carriers on disk are
  the only source of truth.
- **NEVER ALLOCATE A TASK ID FROM THIS FILE** — its highest ID lags the folders, so
  "highest + 1" lands on a live folder and overwrites another session's carrier; names
  TASK_2026_194 as the failure mode and notes it has really happened.
- **CORRECT ALLOCATION** — the `tasks:create` RPC (`TaskWriterService.create`, atomic);
  offline, a folder scan of `.ptah/specs/TASK_*` then an exclusive, fail-if-exists
  `mkdir` as the lock, rescan-and-retry on `EEXIST`.

Everything stays inside `<!-- -->`, so rendered markdown is unchanged.

### Test pinning it

`registry-generator.service.spec.ts` gains `warns in-file against allocating IDs from
the registry`, which asserts on `DERIVED, NOT AUTHORITATIVE`, `NEVER ALLOCATE A TASK ID
FROM THIS FILE`, `tasks:create`, and `fail-if-exists mkdir` — plus a structural check
that every non-blank header line is an HTML comment (catches both "rendered markdown got
polluted" and "someone dropped the warning"). The existing header assertion at `:79` is
unchanged and still passes; the doc comment on the new test records the TASK_2026_264
double-allocation as the reason the warning is load-bearing output rather than a code
comment.

## 2. `registry.md` regenerated through the real code path

Not hand-written. Option 2 from the brief: a throwaway `tmp-regen-registry.ts` +
`tmp-regen-tsconfig.json` at the repo root, run with
`npx tsx --tsconfig tmp-regen-tsconfig.json tmp-regen-registry.ts`. It instantiated the
real `TaskScannerService` and `RegistryGeneratorService` with the real
`CliFileSystemProvider` (`libs/backend/platform-cli`) against `D:/projects/ptah-extension`.
**Both throwaway files have been deleted** — `git status` shows no `tmp-regen*` entries.

Two wrinkles worth recording for whoever does this next:

- `tsx` needs `--tsconfig tsconfig.base.json`; there is no root `tsconfig.json`, so
  without the flag the `@ptah-extension/*` aliases do not resolve.
- The `@ptah-extension/vscode-core` barrel pulls in the `vscode` module, which does not
  exist under plain Node. The temp tsconfig was generated by merging `tsconfig.base.json`'s
  96 paths with `"vscode": ["./libs/backend/cli-engine/src/lib/shims/vscode-shim.ts"]`
  (a child `paths` block replaces rather than merges, hence the generation step).
  `reflect-metadata` must be imported first for tsyringe.

The service reported:

```
{ "registryPath": ".ptah/specs/registry.md", "includedCount": 113, "excludedCount": 0, "changed": true }
```

### Verification numbers

| Check                                         | Result                |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `ls -d .ptah/specs/TASK_* \| wc -l`           | 113                   |
| `grep -c '^\| TASK_' .ptah/specs/registry.md` | 113                   |
| `_Excluded (no valid frontmatter)_`           | 0 folder(s)           |

Row count equals folder count exactly and the generator excluded nothing, so **every
folder on disk has a parseable carrier** — no folder is invisible to the Tasks board, and
nothing needed a carrier edit. (Had one failed to parse I would have stopped rather than
touch someone else's carrier; it did not come up.)

## One thing left open

The warning now lives in the generated artifact, which helps an agent that reads
`registry.md`. It does not help one that never opens the file and guesses from
`registry.md`'s reputation. If you want the hole actually closed rather than signposted,
the follow-up is to make the offline path executable — a `ptah tasks:allocate`-style
command that does the scan + exclusive `mkdir` itself, so there is a thing to run rather
than a paragraph to obey. Out of scope here; flagging it rather than doing it.
